film.title: Nepal Has Hydropower. Why Isn’t It Enough?

home.title: Evidence on Nepal’s electricity system
home.lead: Nepal builds more hydropower every year, yet still imports electricity every winter. This wiki explains why, page by page, with every figure traced to its source and every claim given a confidence rating.

questions.title: Why does Nepal import power in winter?
questions.answer: Most plants run with the river and there is very little storage, so output falls with dry-season flows while demand does not.

questions.title: Who controls the grid?
questions.answer: The Nepal Electricity Authority dispatches the grid, buys most of the electricity and administers contract penalties, while also owning power plants that compete with the producers it judges.

questions.title: What should change?
questions.answer: The constraints are ranked, and the options are compared with the evidence each one still needs.
